Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: My son complains that things look blurry, especially when he's reading or watching TV. We've noticed it's been bothering him more often lately.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He was diagnosed with otitis media last year. The doctor said it was due to a buildup of fluid in his middle ear. Thankfully, it cleared up after treatment.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Lately‚ my son has complained of tooth sensitivity whenever he eats cold foods like ice cream. It seems to be getting worse‚ so I'm worried it might need checking.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: During playtime‚ his breathing gets faster than I expect. As a parent who's had experience with kids‚ it does seem a bit unusual. I'm not sure if it's anything serious though.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain‚ nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: He was slower reaching milestones like walking or sitting compared to his peers. However‚ once he got going‚ he caught up quickly. Still‚ I keep a close eye on how he develops.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Constipation has become a recurring issue. Some days are better than others‚ but it's definitely causing discomfort.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Sometimes‚ he struggles with clarity when trying to speak. His words get jumbled‚ and it takes him a moment to express himself clearly. Also‚ there are those undescended test results we're waiting to hear back about.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected during playtime, which may indicate a potential heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which causes discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach milestones like walking or sitting, and experiences speech difficulties, such as jumbled words and delayed expression.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and many have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was diagnosed with otitis media, which caused a buildup of fluid in the middle ear, and experiences speech difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, especially when reading or watching TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, especially when eating cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and many attend mainstream primary school with additional support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delay and speech difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and speech difficulties
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise, especially if sacral dimple is present

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more easily than other kids her age and needs to rest for a bit longer than her friends do after a short play session.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Feeding has been a difficulty for her since birth, with trouble swallowing certain textures and refusing some foods due to gagging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other children, has poor balance, and struggles to speak clearly with words not always understandable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with otitis media, an inflammation of the middle ear, and has hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes quite often, especially when trying to focus on something, and has eye strain.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods and has difficulty finding toothpaste and foods that don't cause her discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including speech delay and difficulty with balance and coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects her posture and walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism and squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and learning difficulties
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted easily and tires out faster than her peers, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movement problems and frequent stomachaches.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, struggles with balance and movement, and has delayed speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and many have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks for repetitions, suggesting potential hearing issues, and has trouble chewing harder foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints and has trouble seeing straight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech development and struggles with communication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many require special educational support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, struggles with balance and movement, and has delayed speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as short fingers, curved fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and address any dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to assess hearing and address any hearing-related issues.
* Eyesight review to assess vision and address any vision-related issues.
* Cardiac review to assess heart function and address any cardiac concerns.
* Referral for a skeletal review to assess bone health and address any skeletal concerns.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental needs.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if growth is below the 2nd centile.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart with an unspecified abnormality.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties during mealtimes, getting frustrated because eating doesn't always go smoothly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and experiences seizures, which are a significant concern for management and treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in his ear, which is being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things that are far away, indicating potential issues with distance vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring careful monitoring of diet and regular brushing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans at the secondary level.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems behind in development compared to other kids his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe, and many children experiencing behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with his fontanelle not closed properly, which took time to fix.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and others may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess and correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone age and potential skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.
* Management and treatment of epilepsy and seizures.
* Monitoring and potential treatment of heart abnormalities.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets winded easily and needs breaks, indicating potential respiratory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty keeping up with physical activities and gets winded easily, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiac issues, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, are reported in approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely picky about food textures, making mealtime stressful, and has feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly, has coordination issues, and speech delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay, seizures, and neurological issues are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often asking for repetition, and has had issues with ear infections.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media, glue ear, and conductive hearing loss are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, resulting in headaches and vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, including astigmatism, myopia, and hypermetropia, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent dental issues, requiring regular check-ups, and has weak enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delays and may require additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may benefit from special education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, speech delays, and potential behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder and ADHD, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues and potential skeletal problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, including short fingers and curvature of the 5th fingers, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor and address hearing concerns
* Eyesight review to monitor and address vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor and address cardiac concerns
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address delays
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring for signs of tethered cord and consideration of MRI if clinical concerns arise

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Loud noises really overwhelm him. He gets frustrated when there's too much going on around him and often covers his ears to block out the sound. It's hard to see him like that, but I guess it's just his way of coping.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth aren't as strong as they should be. The dentist said he has weak enamel‚ which makes me nervous about cavities and how well he'll take care of them as he grows older.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's something about his heart valve that isn't quite right. I try not to worry too much‚ but it's always there in the back of my mind. The doctors keep an eye on it‚ so I hope that's reassuring enough.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: He experiences epilepsy. It's been a challenge learning how to manage it‚ but we're working closely with his neurologist to find the best approach. Some days are better than others‚ but we're hopeful for his future.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Constipation has been an ongoing issue. He struggles to go regularly‚ and it causes him a lot of discomfort. We've tried different strategies to help‚ but it's still something we're figuring out.

Parent: Sometimes he finds it hard to express himself clearly‚ which leads to frustration for both of us. Also‚ there's an issue with the fontanelle not closing properly‚ but we're waiting for further advice on how to proceed with that.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue that requires close monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, including a strong aversion to certain foods and occasional constipation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which is characterized by weak muscles, and receives physiotherapy to help improve muscle strength.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which can be treated with anti-epileptic medications.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media, an infection in the middle ear, and experiences hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes frequently when trying to focus, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to experience vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences sensitive teeth, particularly when consuming cold food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups crucial.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delay and potential learning difficulties may impact her educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and some may need to attend special schools or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delay and potential learning difficulties may impact her behavior and development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often experience behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to address potential hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart valve issue
* Physiotherapy to help improve muscle strength and address hypotonia
* Occupational therapy to support developmental delay and learning difficulties
* Speech therapy to address potential speech delays
* Behavioral therapy to support behavioral differences and developmental delay

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired pretty quickly when playing outside or running around, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is really picky about food and has a limited diet, making mealtime a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes stares off into space for a few seconds, which may indicate a potential neurological issue, such as seizures, which are reported in around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are at a higher risk of having seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing and often turns the TV up really loud, which may indicate a hearing issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things up close and has been diagnosed with hypermetropia (long-sightedness).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip really easily, requiring frequent dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have weak enamel and may experience a variety of dental concerns, including large front teeth and other dental anomalies.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school and may require special education plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an odd posture when standing or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision and address any vision concerns.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal health.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral concerns.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily, more so than other kids her age, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, which makes mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit clumsy compared to others, and her coordination isn't as good.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear once, but that was treated and seems okay now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs her eyes when she's trying to focus on something, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is prone to cavities and other dental issues, requiring frequent dentist visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and are prone to dental problems, making regular dental check-ups essential.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than usual, and her fontanelle took longer to close than it should have.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental issues
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect any potential hearing problems
* Eyesight review to assess vision and potential vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate potential heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess bone age and potential skeletal issues
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral differences

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Actually, he has a tendency to turn the TV volume up really high. We're not sure if it's related to his hearing or just a habit, but it's something we've noticed consistently.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: He needs to go to the dentist more often than other kids his age. The dentist says his teeth are prone to cavities and other issues, so we have to be super vigilant about his oral hygiene.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's an issue with one of the heart valves. The doctors are keeping an eye on it, and we go for regular check-ups to make sure everything is okay.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He was slower to reach some of the big milestones like walking or sitting. It took him longer than his peers to master these skills, and that was worrying for us.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Parent: Besides the valve issue and feeding challenges, he also has speech delay. His words aren't clear yet, and that's causing frustration for both of us. Additionally, his back has a bit of a curve, which the doctors call scoliosis. We're under guidance from specialists for these conditions too.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, and around 20-40% of people are reported as having seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to turn the TV volume up really high, which may be related to his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which makes it hard for him to see clearly.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay.

* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to monitor vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac review to monitor heart valve issue and address any concerns

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect and is monitored by a cardiologist to prevent the condition from worsening.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, and various strategies have been tried to help regulate bowel movements, with further testing considered if the issue persists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, and a small number require short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic seizures, and works closely with a neurologist to manage the condition and prevent episodes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, and efforts are being made to take better care of his teeth to prevent further issues. The patient also has a speech delay.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more easily than other kids his age, even after short periods of play, which may be related to a heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient does not gain weight as quickly as other kids and has atypical feeding patterns and digestion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has tethered cord, which may cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media (ear infections) and has trouble with his ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and trouble seeing things far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, myopia, and hypermetropia.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs frequent dental visits due to prone teeth and constant monitoring for cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia and palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved 5th fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and prevent cavities
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems
* Check position of testes in boys to address undescended testes
* Consider a palate review to address feeding difficulties or speech concerns
* Referral for a cardiac review to address potential heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to address potential skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral differences

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a small hole in her heart that requires regular check-ups to ensure it does not worsen.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is a recurring issue that requires management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has neurological issues, including frequent falls, tripping over her own feet, and bumping into things, which may indicate issues with muscle tone or coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which can be treated with anti-epileptic medications.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets overwhelmed by loud noises and has difficulty in noisy environments, which may indicate hearing or sensory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints and has trouble seeing straight ahead, which may indicate vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups due to cavity concerns and needs to maintain good oral hygiene.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need to attend special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has unique movement patterns and may have developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects her back and posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curved fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor for cavities and maintain oral hygiene
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the small hole in the heart
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and movement issues
* Monitoring for tethered cord, particularly if sacral dimple is present
* Management of constipation to prevent complications
* Regular monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly, even during simple physical activities, and has scoliosis, which may indicate neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had fluid in her ear last year, affecting her hearing, and tends to squint, which can strain her eyes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and some have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to squint, which can strain her eyes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods, possibly due to weak enamel or a small cavity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to check for heart conditions

* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires regular monitoring and check-ups with cardiologists, and the condition has been managed well with medication and lifestyle adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a sensitive stomach and certain foods trigger discomfort or digestive issues, requiring mindful diet and avoidance of triggers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of unusual staring or blank spells, prompting neurologist consultations to understand and address the issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated in noisy environments and loud noises seem to overwhelm him, leading to tantrums or requests to leave the area.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit very close to the television or when reading books, raising concerns about his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and avoids certain textures or foods that require more effort to chew.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, and regular physical therapy sessions have been beneficial in managing this condition and improving mobility.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and gum health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to assess vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition and adjust treatment as necessary
* Neurological evaluation to understand and address episodes of unusual staring or blank spells
* Physical therapy to manage hip dysplasia and improve mobility
* Occupational therapy to address feeding difficulties and improve fine motor skills
* Speech therapy to address speech delay and improve communication skills
* Behavioural therapy to address behavioural differences and improve coping mechanisms

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties as a baby, but this has improved over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are being managed with the help of a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media in the past and has experienced hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned experiencing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth, which have not been checked by a dentist yet.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties during mealtimes and requires extra effort to ensure he eats well.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids his age, which can be worrying at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is bothered by loud noises and has hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, which affects his vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are not very strong and tend to break or chip easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some experience a variety of other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves differently compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often experience developmental delay, and some may have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves differently compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine, and some experience short fingers or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth strength and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address hearing difficulties
* Eyesight review to assess vision and address any squinting or vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than what's typical for kids his age during playtime, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is a recurring issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and a small number require short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, appearing unbalanced, and has slower developmental progress compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and many have developmental delay, with the degree ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had glue ear, which has required hospital check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which affects their ability to see things far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require more attention than average, necessitating frequent dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups crucial.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's overall development seems slower compared to peers, and they are not saying as many words as expected for their age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower developmental progress and coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may experience developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel condition
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing concerns
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart condition
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental progress and address coordination issues
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular check-ups to address constipation and other gastrointestinal concerns

## 1) RESPIRATORY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an abnormality with their heart valve, as mentioned by a specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble eating sometimes, and it seems to upset their tummy, indicating feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really tired after playing outside for a bit, indicating possible neurological issues related to energy levels.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had a glue ear before, which was treated with medicine, and currently experiences no issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs their eyes a lot, especially when trying to focus, indicating possible vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about sensitive teeth, especially when eating cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some experience a variety of other dental concerns, including large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has short fingers compared to other kids.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart valve abnormality
* Consider referral for a skeletal review to assess spinal and finger abnormalities
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and feeding difficulties

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movement accidents and has unpredictable bowel habits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls over more often than expected, even when not running, and has delayed speech.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing when called from another room and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, which causes discomfort, and does not like wearing glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with some requiring patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth that stick out and are noticeable when smiling.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large permanent teeth, weak enamel, and may require regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to learn new things than her peers and has delayed speech, potentially requiring extra help.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some attending mainstream schools and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and may require extra support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may benefit from medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine, with some experiencing hip dysplasia or delayed closure of the soft spot on the head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth growth and enamel health
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to check for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess for heart conditions
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires medical attention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which can be uncomfortable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit clumsy and lacks coordination, which may indicate neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have difficulties with coordination and balance.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media and may have hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes frequently when trying to focus, which may indicate vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular dental check-ups and has teeth that require a lot of work.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups essential.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need to attend special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has posture issues and an open fontanelle, which may indicate skeletal problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect any potential hearing issues
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect and provide appropriate treatment
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and coordination issues
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) if clinical concerns arise

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition, specifically a septal defect.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby and had trouble eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with running and playing, and falls down more often, suggesting possible neurological or muscular issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties and likes the TV loud, suggesting possible hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, a condition where far-away objects appear too close.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist often to check if everything is okay, suggesting possible dental concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a delayed closure of the soft spot on his head (anterior fontanelle).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Consider referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal health
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and behaviour.
